title: Workflow Orchestrator runs never dispatch: nothing listens for pof-dag-node-ready
instrument: a test that starts a template and asserts a CLI session is created for each root node
evidence: src/stores/taskDAGStore.ts dispatches pof-dag-node-ready; repo grep for pof-dag-node, markNodeRunning, markNodeCompleted finds only taskDAGStore.ts and task-dag-orchestrator.ts
body:
## Summary
Start Workflow creates a run that can never progress, because no code turns a ready node into a CLI session.

## Description
taskDAGStore emits window events pof-dag-node-ready and pof-dag-node-retry (src/stores/taskDAGStore.ts, startCustomWorkflow). A grep of src finds 0 listeners and 0 callers of markNodeRunning or markNodeCompleted outside the store. Roots stay queued, the panel shows 0 done until Cancel, and a reload files the run as Interrupted. Fixed means either wiring a dispatcher (useModuleCLI / TaskFactory, one session per node, completion back to markNodeCompleted) or withdrawing the Start button until it exists.

## Flow
- Evaluator -> Workflow tab -> pick template and module -> Start
- orchestrator.start() queues root nodes and emits node:ready
- store dispatches the window event; no listener
- panel never advances; only Cancel works

## Expected impact
Designers get the supervised pipeline the tab advertises, or stop being offered one. Wiring spawns real CLI sessions, so concurrency and cost need a decision.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a started workflow actually runs
Before: 0 listeners, 0 production callers of markNodeRunning/markNodeCompleted
After: at least 1 dispatcher; each ready node gets a session and reports completion
Method: probe - grep of src; the rung above needs a live CLI run, outside this round
Result: better
Gate: direction

title: Template moduleScope is ignored: all four single-scope templates accept Select All
instrument: owner decision on whether multi-module runs are intended
evidence: src/lib/workflow-templates.ts:171,184,197,210 declare moduleScope single; ModuleSelector.tsx offers every module; hydrateTemplate has a multi-module branch
body:
## Summary
Every built-in template says single, yet the selector and hydrateTemplate both run it across many modules.

## Description
moduleScope is declared on 4 of 4 templates as single (src/lib/workflow-templates.ts:171,184,197,210) and read by 0 production sites; ModuleSelector always offers multi-select and Select All, and hydrateTemplate has a dedicated multi branch. One of the two is wrong. Fixed means either honouring the field in the selector or changing the templates to selected and dropping the unused value.

## Flow
- Pick any template
- Select All enables every module
- hydrateTemplate builds parallel branches despite single

## Expected impact
Designers stop being able to launch a run the template says it does not support, or the field stops lying. Honouring it removes a capability someone may use.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the declared scope matches behaviour
Before: 4 of 4 templates declare single, 0 enforcement sites
After: declared scope and selector agree on 4 of 4
Method: probe - read and grep; which side is right is a product call no gate can decide
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Orchestrator counters miss nodes skipped during advanceDAG
instrument: orchestrator unit test: A fails with B depending on it, assert completedNodes counts B as WorkflowExecution documents
evidence: src/lib/task-dag-orchestrator.ts findReadyNodes marks nodes skipped without recomputeCounters; markNodeCompleted recomputes before advanceDAG; src/types/task-dag.ts documents completedNodes as including skipped
body:
## Summary
A run with a failed dependency finishes with completedNodes short by every node skipped in the last pass.

## Description
markNodeCompleted calls recomputeCounters and then advanceDAG. findReadyNodes (src/lib/task-dag-orchestrator.ts) sets status skipped afterwards with no recompute, and the terminal event snapshots the stale figure, although WorkflowExecution.completedNodes is documented as including skipped. Fixed means recomputing inside advanceDAG before the terminal check. The file is outside this context, so it is carded.

## Flow
- A -> B chain; A fails
- markNodeCompleted recomputes: completed 0, failed 1
- advanceDAG skips B; counters not recomputed
- History shows 0/2 and the panel progress stops at 50 percent

## Expected impact
History and progress totals add up to the node count. Changes the figures of any run with skips, which is the documented meaning.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the counters match their documented meaning
Before: walked A->B with A failed: completedNodes 0, documented value 1
After: completedNodes 1
Method: simulation - case walked by reading the code; an orchestrator test decides it and is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none

title: milestone-deadlines PUT has no operator guard
instrument: route test: PUT without the operator header returns the guard refusal; run every suite importing the route
evidence: src/app/api/milestone-deadlines/route.ts PUT has no requireOperator; commit 2a0d47c1 guards the judge and craft verdict writes in the sibling API
body:
## Summary
The route that writes and deletes roadmap deadlines accepts any local caller.

## Description
PUT in src/app/api/milestone-deadlines/route.ts upserts or deletes a row with no requireOperator, while the wave-22 commit 2a0d47c1 added that guard to verdict writes. Deadlines feed nba-deadline.ts and nba-engine.ts, so a stray write changes prioritisation. Fixed means the same guard plus a client that sends what it requires. The route is outside this context, so it is carded.

## Flow
- Any local process sends PUT /api/milestone-deadlines
- row changes with no operator check
- NBA deadline scoring reads the new value

## Expected impact
Deadlines change only through the operator path. The hook now calls this route through tryApiFetch, so a missing header would surface as a save error.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - only the operator can change deadlines
Before: 0 guard calls in the route
After: 1 guard on PUT
Method: probe - read of the route; the guard test belongs to the API context
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
